criterion: A name stays kernel only when Aura code cannot implement it without losing atomicity or a host effect. Otherwise it is stdlib-candidate, or delete when another registered name already provides the same behaviour.
how_to_change: Every name registered in src must appear here. Adding a registration requires deleting one elsewhere, or listing the new name in kernel_exceptions with a justification. scripts/coverage/checks/check_primitive_tiers_5008.py enforces this; docs/generated/primitives.md is rendered from this file.

rule_notes.K-HOT: hot table in evaluator_primitives_builtins.cpp: native dispatch, no Aura body
rule_notes.K-PANIC: panic checkpoint/restore is atomic workspace state
rule_notes.K-VAL: value model: constructor/accessor/type predicate over a host value representation
rule_notes.K-STR: string heap access/allocation; the engine hash function also keys hash tables
rule_notes.K-NUM: numeric tower: libm host call or IEEE rounding, no Aura body
rule_notes.K-CTRL: control / error / interpreter entry; needs the evaluator itself
rule_notes.K-FFI: host effect: FFI boundary and raw memory
rule_notes.K-HOSTLIB: host library call (regex engine / encoding / byte reinterpretation)
rule_notes.K-WS: atomic interpreter/workspace state; Aura cannot preserve the atomicity it provides
rule_notes.K-ENGINE: engine internals (AST / compile pipeline / type checker / macro hygiene / module loader)
rule_notes.K-FIBER: fiber scheduling / mailbox host state; atomic across fibers
rule_notes.K-GOV: process-level governance / memory / counters (atomic host state)
rule_notes.K-QRY: reads engine-internal indexes (def-use, provenance, AST) under a workspace lock
rule_notes.K-AGENT: agent loop state / strategy registry / LLM host effect
rule_notes.S-PAIR: composition of car/cdr (R7RS defines them in the library)
rule_notes.S-STR: pure string algorithm over string-ref/length; #1440 kept these core for speed, not for semantics
rule_notes.S-PURE: pure value->value function; #1440 kept json-*/string-* core for speed, not for semantics
rule_notes.D-ALIAS: redundant registration: the same behaviour is already reachable through another name
rule_notes.K-EXC-5003: Kernel exceptions added with the SRFI-151 baseline: bitwise/bit-count/arithmetic-shift cannot be expressed in Aura before any bit primitive exists (#5003).
rule_notes.D-PREFIX-5009: retired duplicate prefix (#5009): the same behaviour is the op of one (query …) / (mutate …) verb; kept registered and flagged deprecated for one release cycle
rule_notes.K-ORCH-VERB-5006: orchestration verb: scheduler/mailbox host state; Aura cannot implement it without the fiber scheduler
rule_notes.D-SINGLE-5006: single-use prefix (#5006): the engine name stays for one release cycle as a deprecated alias; the operation is a query/mutate op or a std library function
rule_notes.K-EXC-5006: Kernel exceptions added with the five orchestration verbs (#5006): they replace 24 prefixed orch: names, the deprecated aliases retire next cycle, and no removable name was left in the same change.
rule_notes.D-ORCH-5006: retired orch: prefix (#5006): workflow, supervision, tokens, directory and metrics live in std/orch; keep registered + deprecated for the v0.2.0 alias window
rule_notes.D-BARE-5006: retired bare name (#5006): the name stays registered one release cycle as a deprecated alias; its replacement is a std library function or a query / mutate op
rule_notes.K-FFI-5006: kernel by the FFI host-effect rule (#5006): the c-* family is dlopen/dlsym/native memory, installed only by (require "std/ffi") under effect:ffi; Aura has no expression for a host pointer, so the names stay kernel with std/ffi as their library face (the #3176 deferred-surface contract pins the registration)
rule_notes.K-EXC-5095: add_mutate names are the public write surface (#5095). They were registered before this gate could see them. v0.2.1 counts them; a new add_mutate name still needs a removal or a kernel_exceptions entry.
rule_notes.K-EXC-5096: eof-object is the unique R7RS eof sentinel (#5096). eof-object? already rejects every other value, including void, so a successful write-char is not eof. The constructor has to be the same host value the predicate recognizes; a per-module vector would not be eq? to the primitive. No registration was removable in the stdlib fix.
rule_notes.K-EXC-5118: Restored orch verbs (#5118). #5111 unregistered the scope, workflow, directory and metrics names before std/orch had a body for them. They stay registered and deprecated for one cycle. The doc hint names the function to call (the verb itself, or parallel-intend for orch:parallel-intend). No other registration was removable in the same change.
rule_notes.K-R7RS: R7RS-small required procedure; a conversion spelling exists, but removing this name would break the declared R7RS surface
